page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.12xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a 2.7 GHz base frequency. It is equipped with 192 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 vector support with VNNI and BF16 extensions, alongside dedicated cryptographic acceleration covering AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the upper 25 percent for both single-core and multi-core computational tasks, showing strong scores in Geekbench and PassMark CPU suites. Decompression and code compilation metrics exhibit high parallel scaling, including 260.82 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The memory subsystem records top-decile performance in synthetic memory benchmarks and small-block cached read bandwidth, though large-block uncached memory read and write operations average 111.38 GB/sec and 83.58 GB/sec. Network capacity is defined by a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes no local storage or onboard GPUs, relying on remote block storage for persistence.

With its uniform resource distribution and steady processing metrics, the instance offers consistent resource density for compute-bound and memory-balanced enterprise tasks. High throughput in in-memory transactions is highlighted by 64.56 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance is suited for relational database engines, high-concurrency caching tiers, CI/CD build environments, and containerized backend microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.12xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server offering 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192 GB of RAM on an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at 2.7 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance integrates AVX-512 instructions and hardware cryptographic primitives while maintaining a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes zero local NVMe storage and no GPU accelerators, directing storage operations to network-attached disks. Benchmarks show upper-quartile multi-core and single-core computational output, matched with top-tier memory test results and high-throughput key-value capabilities exceeding 64 million Redis SET operations per second. Although uncached large-block memory transfers settle within median industry ranges, the consistent 1:4 core-to-memory profile delivers dependable throughput across parallel workloads. This configuration is aligned with enterprise application backends, relational databases, continuous integration build clusters, and in-memory caching platforms.
